title: Tech Note: Returning Data Through SOAP
author: David Adams
featured_technology: Get Soap info / native 4D Web server

historical_commentary.text: This note is a thorough, technically detailed guide to 4th Dimension 2003's early SOAP Web Services return-value model — covering the $0 result parameter, the SOAP DECLARATION command for binding process variables/arrays to named XML output elements, supported data type conversions, and practical deployment notes like port numbers and running client/server in separate 4D instances. It is one of the more substantive Tech Notes of the era and remains a valuable historical reference for understanding how 4D bridged its procedural language to XML/SOAP, but the SOAP DECLARATION-based workflow itself has been superseded by 4D's subsequent expansion into REST/JSON web services, which are now the dominant integration model.
related_updates: 4D's web services capabilities expanded significantly beyond SOAP to include REST and JSON-based services with more modern language commands
SOAP DECLARATION and the SOAP-specific request/response model described here are legacy mechanisms rarely used in new 4D development today
4D's native SQL engine (v11 SQL, ~2007) and later ORDA (v16, 2018) changed how data is typically modeled and exposed, further reducing reliance on this era's SOAP-centric data-return patterns
